title: AI Payroll Forecasting
tagline: Predict labor cost before it becomes a cash problem.
summary: Uses payroll history, staff schedules, sales forecasts, and booking volume to estimate upcoming labor cost and labor cost as a percentage of revenue.
businessProblem: Labor is the largest variable cost for most SMBs, but owners only see the true payroll hit after the pay run — too late to adjust schedules or pricing.
outcome: Before each pay period: projected gross payroll, employer taxes, labor-as-% of projected revenue, and flags when labor ratio exceeds your target threshold.
whoItsFor: Appointment-based and shift-based businesses with 3+ employees where labor cost should stay within a defined percentage of revenue.
aiInputs: Sales or booking forecast for the pay period
Target labor cost percentage by business type
Overtime rules and average hourly rates by role
aiOutputs: Projected payroll cost for upcoming pay period
Labor cost as % of projected revenue
Schedule adjustment suggestions to hit target ratio
noCodeTools: Gusto payroll reports + Google Sheets model + ChatGPT
7shifts labor report paste into GPT analysis
Zapier: schedule export → Sheets → weekly GPT summary
lowCodeTools: n8n: Gusto + Square weekly pull → OpenAI labor report
Airtable schedule + payroll tracker with GPT formula
implementationSteps: Define target labor cost % for your business (e.g., 30% for restaurant)
Connect payroll provider and POS/booking data sources
Pull 6 months payroll history to establish baseline
Build pay-period forecast template with schedule hours × rates
Run forecast 3 days before payroll cutoff each cycle
Review accuracy monthly and tune overtime assumptions
systemBehavior: Runs 2–5 days before each scheduled payroll
Does not modify schedules or submit payroll automatically
Compares scheduled hours to historical actuals for sanity check
Alerts only when ratio exceeds threshold — avoids alert fatigue
Planning output only — not payroll tax or compliance filing
risks: Overtime and last-minute schedule changes can invalidate forecasts
Not a substitute for payroll provider calculations or tax compliance
Salaried vs hourly mix requires separate modeling logic
Multi-location businesses need per-location labor targets
